A2c-symmetry

Two animals side by side, clearly separated, both viewed from directly above. Left: a Hydra seen from above, showing its round mouth in the centre and six tentacles spreading out evenly all around like spokes of a wheel (radial symmetry), with four faint thin dashed grey lines crossing through its centre at different angles. Right: an earthworm lying straight and vertical, seen from above, with one faint thin dashed grey line running down the middle from head to tail dividing it into matching left and right halves (bilateral symmetry). Soft greens and pinks.
A2c-tapeworm

A pork tapeworm (Taenia). Left: the whole worm shown as a long flat ribbon arranged in gentle S-shaped loops, starting with a tiny head (scolex) at the top, a narrow neck, then a chain of flat segments (proglottids) that get bigger towards the end. Top right: an enlarged scolex with four round suckers and a crown of curved hooks on a rounded tip (rostellum). Middle right: one enlarged mature proglottid, square, with branching reproductive organs (testes as many dots, ovary, a genital pore on one side). Bottom right: one enlarged gravid proglottid, longer than wide, filled with a branched uterus packed with eggs. Soft creams and pinks.
A2c-tapeworm-life-cycle

Six separate pictures arranged evenly around a large empty circle (clockwise from the top), each a simple illustration with no circle frames or borders around them, white space between them, and no arrows: top: an adult man standing with the outline of his intestine visible containing a long coiled tapeworm; upper right: a small pile of faeces on the ground with tiny white rectangular tapeworm segments in it; lower right: a pig eating from the ground; bottom: an enlarged cross-section of a gut wall with a tiny round embryo bearing EXACTLY SIX small hooks (three pairs) boring through it towards a blood vessel; lower left: a piece of raw pink pork with several small round white cysts (bladder worms) embedded in the muscle; upper left: a plate with a piece of undercooked pork, pink in the middle, and a fork. Soft pinks, creams and browns.
A2c-ascaris

Left: an adult female Ascaris roundworm, long, smooth, cream-pink, cylindrical, tapering at both ends, lying straight and vertical. Middle: a shorter adult male Ascaris, the same colour, lying vertical with its tail end curled into a hook. Right: an enlarged front-on (end-on) view of the head end: a small triangular mouth opening in the centre surrounded by EXACTLY THREE rounded lips, one lip at the top and two lips at the bottom left and bottom right, arranged like a Y (Ascaris always has three lips, never four). Each part clearly separated by white space. Soft pinks and creams.
A2c-earthworm

A large earthworm in side view lying horizontally across the picture, head to the left, on a thin strip of soil. Long body made of many ring-like segments. At the pointed left end a small fleshy lobe (prostomium) overhangs the mouth. About one third of the way from the head, a smooth, swollen, saddle-like band (clitellum) that is a slightly different colour. The blunt right end has the anus. Below the worm, a separate enlarged circular inset showing a few segments from underneath with tiny paired bristles (chaetae) on each segment. Soft pinks and browns.
A2c-mosquito-life-cycle

The life cycle of a mosquito across a single horizontal light blue band of water in the lower half of the picture, with four stages from left to right, evenly spaced, no arrows: 1) a small raft of eggs floating on the water surface; 2) a larva hanging head-down just below the surface, breathing through a short tube at its tail end that touches the surface; 3) a comma-shaped pupa just below the surface with two small breathing trumpets touching the surface; 4) an adult mosquito standing on its empty pupal skin on the water surface. Above the water at the top centre, an adult female mosquito flying. Soft blues, greys and browns.
A2c-cockroach

Dorsal (top) view of an adult cockroach, head at the top, body vertical and symmetrical, shown large. Long thread-like antennae, compound eyes, a broad shield-like pronotum just behind the head, two leathery forewings covering most of the abdomen, three pairs of spiny jointed legs, and a pair of short pointed cerci sticking out at the tail end. Warm reddish-browns.
A2c-housefly-life-cycle

Four separate pictures arranged at the top, right, bottom and left of a large empty circle, with white space between them, no arrows: top: a small cluster of white banana-shaped eggs on a piece of rotting food; right: a white, legless, tapering maggot (larva); bottom: a dark brown barrel-shaped pupa case (puparium); left: an adult housefly seen from above with one pair of clear wings, a grey striped thorax, red eyes and hairy legs. Soft greys, creams and browns.
A2c-honeybee

An adult worker honey bee in side view, head to the left, shown large. Hairy body divided into head, thorax and abdomen; dark and golden bands across the abdomen; a large compound eye; elbowed antennae; a long extended tongue (proboscis) under the head; two pairs of clear veined wings; three pairs of legs, with a round yellow pollen load packed in the pollen basket on the hind leg; and a small sting at the tip of the abdomen. Warm golds, browns and soft blues.
A2c-butterfly-life-cycle

Four separate pictures arranged at the top, right, bottom and left of a large empty circle, with white space between them, no arrows: top: a few small round eggs on a green leaf; right: a green caterpillar eating a leaf, clearly showing three pairs of small jointed true legs at the front and fleshy stumpy prolegs further back; bottom: a green chrysalis (pupa) hanging from a twig; left: an adult butterfly with large, brightly coloured open orange and black wings and clubbed antennae, feeding on a flower. Soft greens, oranges and yellows.
A2c-snail

A giant African land snail in side view gliding to the left along a horizontal leaf, shown large. A big brown spirally coiled shell with darker stripes. A soft grey-brown body with a broad flat muscular foot leaving a faint shiny slime trail on the leaf. On the head two pairs of tentacles: a longer upper pair with dark eyes at their tips and a shorter lower pair. A small round breathing pore visible under the edge of the shell on the right side of the body. Soft browns and creams.
A2c-tilapia

A bony fish (Tilapia) in side view facing left, shown large. Streamlined body covered with overlapping scales; a bony gill cover (operculum) behind the head; a terminal mouth; a large eye without eyelids; a small nostril on the snout; a dotted lateral line running along the side; a long spiny dorsal fin on the back; a pectoral fin just behind the gill cover; a pelvic fin underneath; an anal fin near the tail; and a tail (caudal) fin. Soft silver-greys and blues.
A2c-toad-frog

A toad and a frog side by side, both in side view facing left, clearly separated. Left: a squat brown toad with dry, warty skin, a large oval parotid gland bulge behind each eye, and short hind legs. Right: a slender green frog with smooth, moist, shiny skin, a round eardrum (tympanum) behind the eye, long powerful hind legs and fully webbed hind feet. Soft browns and greens.
A2c-frog-life-cycle

Seven separate pictures arranged evenly around a large empty circle (clockwise from the top), with white space between them, no arrows: top: a clump of frog spawn (black dots in clear jelly) in a little water; then a young tadpole with feathery external gills; then a tadpole with a long tail and no external gills; then a tadpole with small hind legs; then a tadpole with all four legs and a shrinking tail; then a small froglet with a stump of tail climbing onto a stone; then an adult frog on land. Soft greens and blues.
A2c-agama

Two Agama lizards on a flat rock, clearly separated. Left, larger: a male Agama lizard with a bright orange-red head and front part of the tail, dark blue-black body, long tail, four limbs with clawed toes, and a visible ear opening behind the jaw. Right, smaller: a brown female Agama with lighter spots on her sides. Warm oranges, blues and browns.
A2c-bird-mammal

Two panels side by side, clearly separated. Left: a domestic hen standing, showing feathers, beak, wings, scaly legs with clawed toes, and next to her a straw nest with three eggs. Right: a West African dwarf goat mother standing, with hair and external ears, and her kid suckling milk from her udder. Warm creams, browns and soft greens.
A2c-vertebrate-evolution

A left-to-right rising landscape from water to dry land: far left, a fish swimming in blue water; next, a frog sitting at the water's edge; next, a lizard on a dry rock higher up; far right at the top, on dry grassy land, a bird (hen) and a goat. The ground rises like a gentle slope from the water on the left to dry land on the right. Each animal clearly separated. Soft blues, greens and browns.
